children: received an Equal-weight rating as Morgan Stanley initiated coverage on the industrial software platform.
The company is a recent spin-off of the Sweden-based Hexagon

"As a separate, stand-alone company, Octave will have the depth, scale, and expertise necessary to capitalize on software and services opportunities across the industrial and public sector spaces and deliver intelligence at scale," said Octave CEO Mattias Stenberg.
Octave made its initial public offering on the Nasdaq in May 2026.

"Octave is one of the more differentiated industrial software spins in recent years with mission-critical infrastructure exposure, meaningful recurring revenue, high retention, and a large installed-base expansion runway," said Morgan Stanley analyst Elizabeth Porter in a Thursday investor report.
Morgan Stanley set a $21 price target on the stock.

"Octave's recent spin from Hexagon combines Design, Build, Operate, and Protect assets into a ~$1.6B revenue company with ~$1.1B+ ARR, ~70% recurring mix, 97% GRR, 105% NRR, ~30% adjusted operating margin, and ~20% FCF margin," Porter noted. "The valuation debate centers on whether Octave can show its product-line integration is far enough along and its salesforce ready enough to drive the cross-sell that accelerates ARR growth and improves recurring-revenue quality and FCF."

"We expect initial investor skepticism given modest recent organic growth, the ongoing SaaS transition, perpetual-license runoff exposure, muted NRR expansion, and limited stand-alone operating history," she added.

title: Octave initiated at Equal-weight on SaaS transition risk: Morgan Stanley
